_doc: What may be written on a social image, in a caption and in alt text. Shared by scripts/textrules.py (the gate) and src/lib/kit/social.js (the server's second look; its vitest test fails when the two differ, and both run tests/textrules_fixtures.json). Matching is on tokens: accents dropped, lowercase, '&' read as 'and', only a-z and 0-9 runs kept. An image line is sourced when its tokens appear in that order, contiguously, inside one source text of the brief, or when they equal one of the phrases (a phrase that needs 'booking' or 'phone' only when the brief's links have it; one that needs 'quote' only on an image that carries a quote from the pasted reviews). A claim is a number or one of the claim phrases, once the neutral phrases are taken out. Every claim in a line, caption or alt text must also appear in a claimSources text (the business facts or the owner's intake answers), never only in copy we wrote (site, words). Reviews back nothing on their own: a quote role line is one or more whole sentences of one line of the pasted reviews (a quote never joins two reviews), a cite is a run of their words from the quote's own line or from a name line right under it (one sentence of at most 4 words: the reviewer of that quote), and a caption or alt text may quote whole review sentences inside quotation marks.
